answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with burnable service-receipt admission. First, a new agent completes verified jobs, such as data checks, and each job mints one receipt. Second, admission to paid work requires burning 50 receipts, about 200 hours of real service. Third, receipts decay after 30 idle days, so hoarded identities fade. A forger minting 1,000 fake agents would need 50,000 receipts, roughly $180,000 in compute and wages, before earning a cent. Like basalt beneath a velvet rope, the barrier stays quiet yet unyielding, and each honest record reads as one sonnet of proven work.
